records.claim: Gulf crude, condensate and refined-fuel flows excluding Iran averaged about 81% of pre-war levels in September; crude and condensate recovered to 91%, while refined products remained around 60%.
records.observation: The recovery is strongly asymmetric: upstream physical flow has adapted faster than downstream product supply.
records.assessment: PERSISTENT / ADAPTING; reinforces the existing refined-products bottleneck.

records.claim: Oil prices eased as stronger Middle Eastern exports and the G7 emergency stock release reduced immediate supply concern while security risk remained.
records.observation: The October 2 policy delta is propagating into the market as a buffer rather than creating a new system transition.

records.claim: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said methane exporters would receive one additional year of flexibility under EU methane regulation.
records.observation: This is a clear policy signal but not yet evidence that the legal timetable has been formally amended.

records.source: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine / Ministry of Energy
records.claim: Ukraine announced CIF approval of a $116.2 million Renewable Energy Integration investment plan covering cross-border interconnection, renewable generation and storage, including a Chernivtsi–Suceava 400 kV interconnector and a 610 MW BESS window.
records.observation: Secondary reporting dates the CIF board endorsement to October 2; it is therefore treated as late evidence rather than a fresh October 6 delta.
records.assessment: LATE EVIDENCE / BACKDATE, NOT TODAY'S DELTA.
